dictionary.definition: I, me, my; our, us

etymology.hint: A hand 扌 holding a weapon 戈

currentComponents.note: Originally depicted a hand 扌 gripping a weapon 戈; this original meaning was later borrowed to represent the pronoun 'I/we.'

dictionary.definition: plural marker for pronouns and some nouns

etymology.hint: people

currentComponents.note: 亻 (person) — 们 attaches to pronouns and nouns referring to people to mark plural, e.g. 我们 ('we'), 你们 ('you all')
门 (mén) gives a sound close to 们's reading (men)

dictionary.definition: what? mixed, miscellaneous

etymology.hint: A file of ten 十 people 亻

currentComponents.note: 亻 (person) — 什 originally referred to a group of people.
十 (ten) — combined with 亻 (person), 什 originally described a group of ten; the character later came to be used for the common word 什么 (what).

dictionary.definition: interrogative particle

currentComponents.note: 么 derives from 幺, a pictograph of a small twisted skein of silk thread, symbolizing something tiny or insignificant. As a standalone character it was later borrowed purely for its sound, becoming the light, toneless question particle seen in words like 什么 and 怎么.

dictionary.definition: to know, to perceive, to comprehend

etymology.hint: mouth

currentComponents.note: 口 (mouth) — 知 relates to speaking what one knows.
矢 (shǐ) gives a hint of the sound — 知 is pronounced zhī, a connection that has faded over time.

dictionary.definition: method, way; path, road

etymology.hint: walk

currentComponents.note: 辶 (to walk) — 道 relates to a path or road one walks along.
首 (shǒu) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer resembles dào, a reminder that sound components can drift after thousands of years of pronunciation change.

dictionary.definition: other, another; he, she, it

etymology.hint: An additional, "also" 也  person 亻

currentComponents.note: 亻 (person) plus 也 (also/additionally) — historically meant 'another person,' which developed into the third-person pronoun 'he/him.'

dictionary.definition: one; a, an; alone

etymology.hint: Represents heaven (天), earth (旦), or the number 1

currentComponents.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.

dictionary.definition: this, that; single; measure word for individuals

etymology.hint: A tally 丨 of people 人

currentComponents.note: 丨 (a vertical tally mark) over 人 (person) — suggests counting people one by one, fitting 个's role today as Mandarin's most common general measure word.

dictionary.definition: you, second person pronoun

etymology.hint: Pronoun 尔 for a person 亻

currentComponents.note: 亻 (person) plus 尔 (an old second-person pronoun) — combines to form 你, the modern word for 'you.'

dictionary.definition: not, none, gone; to bury; to sink, to drown

etymology.hint: water

currentComponents.note: 氵 (water) — 没 originally meant to sink or drown in water, later extended to the negative 'not have.'
殳 (shū) is the historical sound component; it no longer rhymes with méi in modern Mandarin, another case of sound drift over time.

dictionary.definition: to have, to own, to possess; to exist

currentComponents.note: 月 (yuè) here actually derives from 肉 (meat) — 有 originally depicted a hand holding meat, meaning 'to possess'; it also lends a loose phonetic connection to yǒu.

dictionary.definition: this, these; such; here

usedInWords.meaning: variant of 這裡|这里[zhe4 li3]

currentComponents.note: 辶 (to walk, move) — 这 relates to indicating something nearby, pointing at it as one moves toward it.
文 (wén) is the simplified phonetic element, replacing the traditional 言 found in 這; neither reading closely matches 这's modern pronunciation zhè today.

dictionary.definition: what? why? how?

etymology.hint: heart

currentComponents.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 怎's meaning 'how' relates to a mental inquiry, what's on one's mind.
乍 (zhà) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from zěn.

dictionary.definition: to appear, to manifest; current, now

etymology.hint: To see 见 jade 王; 见 also provides the pronunciation

currentComponents.note: 王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — a valuable object one might glimpse or notice.
见 (to see) — catching sight of something links to the meanings 'to appear, present, now.'

dictionary.definition: at, in, on; to exist; used to indicate the present progressive tense

etymology.hint: earth

usedInWords.meaning: to be in the process of

currentComponents.note: 土 (earth/soil) — 在 originally related to standing on the ground
才 (cái) gives the sound — 在 is pronounced zài, a close match

dictionary.definition: may, can, -able; possibly

etymology.hint: vigorous

currentComponents.note: 丁 (a stylized handle/hook shape in the ancient form) — part of the character's original picture, now mostly opaque in the modern form
口 (kǒu, mouth) gives a sound related to 可's pronunciation kě, and may connect to 可's sense of approval spoken aloud

dictionary.definition: according to; so as to; because of; then

currentComponents.note: 以 traces back to an ancient pictograph of a person bent over holding a tool or plough. The image of a person using an implement gave rise to its meaning 'to use, by means of, according to.'

dictionary.definition: as, as if, like, such as, supposing

etymology.hint: A wife 女 following her husband's words 口

currentComponents.note: 女 (woman) — depicts a wife in the traditional image behind this character.
口 (mouth/words) — the wife following her husband's spoken words gave 如 its meaning of 'as, like, if.'

dictionary.definition: fruit, nut; result

etymology.hint: Fruit 田 growing on a tree 木

currentComponents.note: 田 (here representing round fruit, not its usual meaning 'field') — 果 pictures fruit hanging from branches.
木 (tree) — fruit growing on a tree gave 果 its meaning 'fruit' and, more broadly, 'result.'

dictionary.definition: form, pattern, shape, style

etymology.hint: tree

currentComponents.note: 木 (tree/wood) — 样 originally referred to a kind of tree, later broadening to mean 'kind, appearance, way.'
羊 (yáng) gives the sound — 样 is pronounced yàng, matching aside from tone.

dictionary.definition: to tell, to inform, to announce; to accuse

etymology.hint: To speak 口 with the force of an ox 牛

currentComponents.note: 口 (mouth) — the act of speaking.
牛 (ox) — traditionally read as speaking with the forceful weight of an ox, giving 告 its meaning 'to tell, announce, inform.'

dictionary.definition: to accuse, to sue; to inform; to narrate

etymology.hint: Words 讠 of blame 斥; 斥 also provides the pronunciation

currentComponents.note: 讠 (speech) — represents words being spoken.
斥 (to reprimand, blame) — words of accusation or complaint gave 诉 its meaning 'to sue, to tell, to complain.'

dictionary.definition: cause, reason; by; because

currentComponents.note: 囗 (an enclosure) surrounds the character.
大 (a person with arms outstretched) sits inside the enclosure — a picture of someone relying on their surroundings, giving 因 its senses 'to rely on' and, by extension, 'cause, reason.'

dictionary.definition: to do, to act; to handle, to govern; to be

currentComponents.note: 为's traditional form 為 depicted a hand grasping the trunk of an elephant, symbolizing training an elephant to work — the source of 为's meaning 'to do, to act,' and by extension 'for, because of.'

dictionary.definition: self; private, personal; from

etymology.hint: A nose; in China, people refer to themselves by pointing to their noses

currentComponents.note: A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'

dictionary.definition: self, oneself; personal, private; 6th heavenly stem

etymology.hint: A loom woven with thread

currentComponents.note: 己 is thought to depict a woven cord or thread pattern, though its exact original picture is debated; it came to be used for the reflexive idea of 'oneself.'

dictionary.definition: unit of distance equal to 0.5km; village; lane

etymology.hint: Unit of measure for farm 田 land 土

usedInWords.meaning: variant of 這裡|这里[zhe4 li3]
variant of 裡面|里面[li3 mian4]

currentComponents.note: 田 (farmland) over 土 (earth/soil) — originally referred to a village or a measured unit of farmland, later extended to mean 'inside' or a unit of distance.

dictionary.definition: only; but, however, yet, still

currentComponents.note: 旦 (dàn) gives the sound — 但 is also pronounced dàn, an exact match.

dictionary.definition: to be; indeed, right, yes; okay

etymology.hint: To speak 日 directly 疋

currentComponents.note: Traditionally analyzed as 日 combined with 疋, linked to the idea of speaking directly and truthfully — the source of 是's meaning 'to be, indeed, right.'

dictionary.definition: time, season; period, era, age

etymology.hint: day

currentComponents.note: 日 (sun/day) — relates to 时's meaning of 'time, season'; the phonetic part of the character was later replaced by 寸 in the simplified form

dictionary.definition: to wait, to expect; to visit; to greet

etymology.hint: person

currentComponents.note: 亻 (person) — relates to 候's meaning 'to wait, time,' as if a person watching and waiting.
矦 (hóu) gives a sound hint — 候 is pronounced hòu, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

dictionary.definition: already; finished; to stop; then, afterwards

currentComponents.note: 已 began as a pictograph closely related to 巳, showing a coiled snake or a tied-off cord. The character was later borrowed phonetically to write the grammatical sense 'already, to stop, to cease,' unrelated to its original picture.

dictionary.definition: the classics; to experience, to undergo

etymology.hint: thread

currentComponents.note: 纟 (silk/thread) — 经 originally referred to the vertical warp threads in weaving.
工 (gōng) gives a related sound cue for 经 (jīng), reflecting an older, closer pronunciation link between the two.

dictionary.definition: to thank; to refuse politely

etymology.hint: speech

currentComponents.note: 讠 (speech) — 谢 describes an act of speaking, giving thanks.
射 (shè) gives the sound — an exact match with 谢.

dictionary.definition: conscious; to nap, to sleep; to wake up

etymology.hint: see

currentComponents.note: 见 (to see, perceive) — relates to 觉's meaning 'to feel, sense, perceive.'
⺍ is a small graphic element serving as the phonetic hint, though its link to jué's modern sound has faded after centuries of change.

dictionary.definition: to obtain, to get, to acquire; suitable, proper; ready

etymology.hint: A hand 寸 grabbing a shell 旦

currentComponents.note: 寸 (a hand) reaching for 旦 (originally 貝, a shell used as currency) — a picture of grasping something valuable, hence 'to obtain, to get.'

dictionary.definition: first, former, previous

etymology.hint: Someone stepping 止 in front of another person 儿

currentComponents.note: 止 (a foot, stepping forward) — 先 pictures someone moving ahead of another.
儿 (a person) — one person stepping ahead of another gave 先 its meaning 'before' or 'first.'

dictionary.definition: life, lifetime; birth; growth

etymology.hint: A shoot 屮 growing in the soil 土

currentComponents.note: 屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.

dictionary.definition: to love; to enjoy, to be happy; joyful, glad

etymology.hint: Singing 口 and beating drums 壴

currentComponents.note: 壴 (a drum) — beating a drum in celebration
口 (mouth) — singing along in celebration

dictionary.definition: happy, glad, joyful

currentComponents.note: 又 replaced the more complex phonetic component 雚 (guān) when 欢 was simplified from the traditional 歡; it keeps only a loose echo of that original sound, now read huān.
欠 depicts a person with an open mouth, as if yawning or gasping — an image of an open, expressive face that connects to 欢's meaning of joy and delight.

dictionary.definition: can, may; capable, full of energy

etymology.hint: A bear's head 厶, body ⺼, and claws 匕

currentComponents.note: Originally a drawing of a bear, with 厶 as its head, ⺼ as its body, and 匕匕 as its claws; the picture was later borrowed to mean 'ability, to be able to.'

dictionary.definition: to need, to require; must

etymology.hint: Rain 雨 needed for crops to grow

currentComponents.note: 雨 (rain) — something crops require to grow, giving 需 its meaning 'to need, require.'

dictionary.definition: essential, necessary; to ask for; to coerce; to demand

etymology.hint: A woman 女 with hands on her waist 覀

currentComponents.note: 女 (woman) with 覀 depicting hands on the waist — an old image of insisting or demanding something, connected to 要's meaning 'to want, to need.'

dictionary.definition: aim, goal; of; possessive particle; -self suffix

currentComponents.note: 白 (white, bright) — 的's original meaning was a bright, white spot, as in the white center of an archery target, giving 的 its old meaning 'target, bullseye.'
勺 supplies the character's original sound reading dí, distinct from the common possessive-particle reading de that the character carries today.

dictionary.definition: that, that one, those

currentComponents.note: 阝 (a mound, used in place names) anchors 那 as originally the name of a location. Over time the character was borrowed away from that place name to serve as the demonstrative pronoun 'that,' the meaning it carries in modern words like 那位 and 那儿.

The left-hand element is close in sound to nà and supplied the original pronunciation for the place name. That phonetic role is the only reason it survives in the modern character, since its literal meaning was lost long ago.

dictionary.definition: east, eastern, eastward

etymology.hint: Simplified form of 東, the sun 日 rising behind a tree 木

currentComponents.note: 东 (simplified from 東) originally pictured the sun 日 rising behind a tree 木 — since the sun rises in the east, the character came to mean 'east.'

dictionary.definition: west, western, westward

etymology.hint: A bird settling into its nest, representing sunset; compare 東

currentComponents.note: 西 is thought to depict a bird settling into its nest at dusk — since birds return to roost as the sun sets in the west, the character came to mean 'west.'

dictionary.definition: should, must; to respond, to handle; to deal with, to cope

currentComponents.note: The base of 应 preserves a trace of 心 (heart, mind), reflecting the traditional 應's link to an inner, felt reaction — the root of meanings like 'to respond' and 'to answer.'
应 simplifies 應, whose original phonetic element was a bird-related term read yīng; that ancient reading survives in one of 应's two modern pronunciations, yīng, as in 应该 (yīnggāi, 'should').

dictionary.definition: should, ought to, must

etymology.hint: speech

currentComponents.note: 讠 (speech) — relates to 该's meaning 'ought to, should,' as if reached through spoken agreement.
亥 (hài) gives a sound hint — 该 is pronounced gāi, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant and tone differ.
